    # Keep deterministic: no randomness

    def route_load(route):
        s = 0
        for node in route:
            s += demands[node]
        return s

    def route_cost(route):
        if not route:
            return 0
        c = matrix[depot][route[0]] + matrix[route[-1]][depot]
        for a, b in zip(route, route[1:]):
            c += matrix[a][b]
        return c

    def total_cost(routes):
        return sum(route_cost(r) for r in routes)

    # --- Edit 1 (focused): better deterministic construction via Clarke-Wright savings (capacity-feasible merges) ---
    customer_ids = list(customers_set)
    # Sort deterministically for reproducibility even before savings
    customer_ids.sort()

    hint = instance.get("vehicle_count_hint", 0) or 0
    target_vehicles = hint if hint > 0 else len(customer_ids)

    # Initialize as singleton routes (each customer served by one vehicle)
    routes = []
    route_loads = []
    route_of = [-1] * (len(demands))
    # Also store orientation canonical: route lists can be reversed during merge
    for cid in customer_ids:
        r = [cid]
        routes.append(r)
        rl = demands[cid]
        route_loads.append(rl)
        route_of[cid] = len(routes) - 1

    def savings(i, j):
        return matrix[depot][i] + matrix[depot][j] - matrix[i][j]

    # Compute and sort savings pairs
    # To control size: use nearest_neighbors if available
    nn = instance.get("nearest_neighbors", {})
    pairs = []
    use_nn = isinstance(nn, dict) and len(nn) > 0
    if use_nn:
        # Build candidate pairs using top-N neighbors (bounded and deterministic)
        # Fallback if key missing: will not add pair
        # Choose small N to keep runtime down, but large enough to help bottlenecks
        N = 20
        seen = set()
        for i in customer_ids:
            key = str(i)
            if key in nn:
                for j in nn[key][:N]:
                    if j in customers_set and j != i:
                        a, b = (i, j) if i < j else (j, i)
                        if (a, b) not in seen:
                            seen.add((a, b))
                            pairs.append((a, b))
        # If nn filtering is too aggressive, add a few more pairs deterministically from depot distance order
        if len(pairs) < min(5000, len(customer_ids) * 5):
            # add pairs between first K closest-to-depot customers and others
            closest = sorted(customer_ids, key=lambda x: (matrix[depot][x], demands[x], x))
            K = min(len(closest), 30)
            base = closest[:K]
            for i in base:
                for j in closest:
                    if i != j and (i, j) not in [(min(i, j), max(i, j))]:
                        a, b = (i, j) if i < j else (j, i)
                        if (a, b) not in [(min(i, j), max(i, j))]:
                            if (a, b) not in set(pairs):
                                pairs.append((a, b))
    if not pairs:
        # Full pair set (may be large, but bounded by keeping few hundred via hint)
        # Deterministic scan: sort by depot distance to limit to top-L customers for savings
        L = len(customer_ids)
        if hint > 0:
            # more vehicles => allow more pairs
            L = min(len(customer_ids), max(60, 3 * hint))
        depot_order = sorted(customer_ids, key=lambda x: (matrix[depot][x], demands[x], x))
        focus = depot_order[:L]
        set_focus = set(focus)
        for i in focus:
            for j in focus:
                if i < j and j in set_focus:
                    pairs.append((i, j))

    # Sort savings decreasing; deterministic tie break by i,j
    # Each pair is stored as (i,j) with i<j
    pairs.sort(key=lambda p: (-savings(p[0], p[1]), p[0], p[1]))

    def find_route_idx(cid):
        return route_of[cid]

    # Attempt merges: only allow merging when i is tail of route A and j is head of route B (or reversed)
    # We will merge at endpoints; if route directions don't match, we reverse one route to make it match.
    route_active = [True] * len(routes)
    current_vehicle_count = len(routes)

    for i, j in pairs:
        ri = find_route_idx(i)
        rj = find_route_idx(j)
        if ri == -1 or rj == -1 or ri == rj:
            continue
        if not route_active[ri] or not route_active[rj]:
            continue
        if current_vehicle_count <= target_vehicles:
            break  # don't over-merge when vehicles already adequate

        # Decide which merge orientation yields i-tail and j-head
        # Consider four endpoint cases:
        # 1) i is tail of ri and j is head of rj => append
        # 2) i is tail of ri and j is tail of rj => reverse rj then append
        # 3) i is head of ri and j is head of rj => reverse ri then append
        # 4) i is head of ri and j is tail of rj => reverse both then append
        a = routes[ri]
        b = routes[rj]
        i_is_head = (a[0] == i)
        i_is_tail = (a[-1] == i)
        j_is_head = (b[0] == j)
        j_is_tail = (b[-1] == j)
        if not (i_is_head or i_is_tail) or not (j_is_head or j_is_tail):
            continue

        # capacity check
        if route_loads[ri] + route_loads[rj] > capacity:
            continue

        # choose merge operation deterministically
        # Prefer to avoid reversals when multiple orientations are possible
        did = False
        # Case 1: i tail, j head
        if i_is_tail and j_is_head:
            # a + b
            a.extend(b)
            load_new = route_loads[ri] + route_loads[rj]
            route_loads[ri] = load_new
            route_active[rj] = False
            current_vehicle_count -= 1
            # update route_of for nodes in b
            for node in b:
                route_of[node] = ri
            routes[rj] = []
            did = True
        # Case 2: i tail, j tail => reverse b, then append
        elif i_is_tail and j_is_tail:
            b.reverse()
            a.extend(b)
            route_loads[ri] = route_loads[ri] + route_loads[rj]
            route_active[rj] = False
            current_vehicle_count -= 1
            for node in b:
                route_of[node] = ri
            routes[rj] = []
            did = True
        # Case 3: i head, j head => reverse a, then append
        elif i_is_head and j_is_head:
            a.reverse()
            a.extend(b)
            route_loads[ri] = route_loads[ri] + route_loads[rj]
            route_active[rj] = False
            current_vehicle_count -= 1
            for node in b:
                route_of[node] = ri
            routes[rj] = []
            did = True
        # Case 4: i head, j tail => reverse both, then append
        elif i_is_head and j_is_tail:
            a.reverse()
            b.reverse()
            a.extend(b)
            route_loads[ri] = route_loads[ri] + route_loads[rj]
            route_active[rj] = False
            current_vehicle_count -= 1
            for node in b:
                route_of[node] = ri
            routes[rj] = []
            did = True
        # Note: if did remains False, skip

        if did:
            # If we merged into ri, keep the list reference already in routes[ri]
            pass

    # Compact routes: remove inactive/empty
    routes = [r for r in routes if r]
    # Recompute loads for safety (still deterministic)
    loads = [route_load(r) for r in routes]

    # --- Original local search code path preserved below (with minor safe edits) ---
    base_total = total_cost(routes)

    # Phase 1: inter-route relocate (1-0 move) with best insertion position
    def best_insertion_cost(route, node):
        # returns (best_pos, best_delta_cost) relative to current route cost,
        # or (None, large) if no feasible insertion
        n = len(route)
        if n == 0:
            # inserting into empty route: depot->node->depot
            return 0, (matrix[depot][node] + matrix[node][depot])
        base = route_cost(route)
        best_pos = None
        best_delta = 10**30
        # Try positions 0..n (insert before index)
        for pos in range(n + 1):
            if pos == 0:
                prev = depot
                nxt = route[0]
                new_cost = matrix[prev][node] + matrix[node][nxt]
                old_cost = matrix[prev][nxt]
                delta = new_cost - old_cost
            elif pos == n:
                prev = route[-1]
                nxt = depot
                delta = (matrix[prev][node] + matrix[node][nxt]) - matrix[prev][nxt]
            else:
                prev = route[pos - 1]
                nxt = route[pos]
                delta = (matrix[prev][node] + matrix[node][nxt]) - matrix[prev][nxt]
            if delta < best_delta - 1e-12 or (abs(delta - best_delta) <= 1e-12 and (best_pos is None or pos < best_pos)):
                best_delta = delta
                best_pos = pos
        return best_pos, best_delta

    # Phase 2: intra-route 2-opt (deterministic first improvement)
    def two_opt_first_improve(route):
        n = len(route)
        if n < 4:
            return False
        for i in range(n - 3):
            a = route[i]
            for j in range(i + 2, n - 1):
                b = route[i + 1]
                c = route[j]
                d = route[j + 1]
                delta = (matrix[a][c] + matrix[b][d]) - (matrix[a][b] + matrix[c][d])
                if delta < -1e-12:
                    route[i + 1:j + 1] = reversed(route[i + 1:j + 1])
                    return True
        return
